questions.text: What is the minimum thickness for the scratch coat in a 3-coat Portland cement plaster system over metal lath under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215?

options.text: 6–8 mm
3–5 mm

questions.rationale: The three-coat system: scratch (9–10 mm, keying through mesh) → brown (10–12 mm, leveling) → finish (3–5 mm, surface). Total: 22–27 mm. Each coat has a specific structural or aesthetic function.

questions.text: What is the critical distinction between how Sec. 1215 in the basic 1977 PD 1096 law and the 2004 Revised IRR differ in their treatment of lath, plaster, and gypsum wall board?

options.text: The basic law and the IRR are identical in their treatment of these materials, offering no changes over time

The basic law delegates material specifications to the Secretary; the 2004 IRR operationalizes this by tying installation requirements to both fire-resistive ratings (Rule VI) and type of construction (Rule IV)
The basic law specifies exact plaster thicknesses; the IRR removes all prescriptive requirements, allowing for flexibility
The 2004 IRR prohibits the use of gypsum wall board entirely in favor of traditional plaster, emphasizing durability

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 is the connector provision — it links the fire-resistive framework (Rule VI), the construction type framework (Rule IV), and the actual installation of wall finishes. Exam questions on this section test the ability to trace these cross-references.

questions.text: What are the coat thicknesses for a 2-coat gypsum plaster system over gypsum lath, and what is the total combined thickness under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215?

options.text: Scratch coat: 9–10 mm; Brown coat: 10–12 mm; Total: 19–22 mm
Base coat: 6–8 mm; Finish coat: 3–5 mm; Total: 9–13 mm
Base coat: 9–10 mm; Finish coat: 3–5 mm; Total: 12–15 mm
Scratch coat: 6–8 mm; Brown coat: 3–5 mm; Total: 9–13 mm

questions.rationale: The number of coats depends on substrate: metal lath requires 3 coats (scratch keying through mesh); gypsum lath or masonry requires 2 coats (no scratch needed because substrate provides bond).

questions.text: What is the standard minimum weight of expanded metal lath for wall applications, and what is the total thickness of a 3-coat Portland cement plaster system over metal lath under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215?

options.text: Expanded metal lath: minimum 1.85 kg/m² for walls; 3-coat plaster total: 22–27 mm
Expanded metal lath: minimum 2.4 kg/m² for walls; 3-coat plaster total: 22–27 mm
Expanded metal lath: minimum 2.4 kg/m² for walls; 3-coat plaster total: 11–15 mm
Expanded metal lath: minimum 1.36 kg/m² for walls; 3-coat plaster total: 15–20 mm

questions.rationale: The three-coat system is mandatory over metal lath: scratch coat (mechanical key), brown coat (leveling), finish coat (surface). The scratch coat is forced through the mesh to create a mechanical key — this is why metal lath requires three coats, while gypsum lath needs only two.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215, which plaster type is appropriate for interior humid areas (but not wet areas), and what is its typical mix?

options.text: Keene's cement — factory mix of burnt gypsum and alum; used in 2 coats for hard, dense interior finish
Portland cement plaster — mixed at 1:3 to 1:4 cement:sand; suitable for humid interior areas
Lime plaster — mixed at 1:2 to 1:3 lime:sand; sets by carbonation and is ideal for humid interior spaces
Gypsum plaster — pre-mixed at 1:2 ratio; used in 2 coats for interior finish in humid environments

questions.rationale: The hierarchy: Portland cement = exterior + wet areas. Gypsum plaster = interior dry areas. Keene's cement = interior humid areas (not wet). Lime plaster = interior dry areas (slow setting). 'Humid' (high moisture but not saturated) vs. 'wet' (direct water exposure) is a critical distinction.

questions.text: What is the minimum thickness of Portland cement plaster for the finish coat in a 3-coat system over metal lath under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215?

options.text: 3–5 mm
6–8 mm

questions.rationale: 3-coat over metal lath: scratch (9–10 mm) → brown (10–12 mm) → finish (3–5 mm) = 22–27 mm total. The finish coat is intentionally thin — its function is surface texture and aesthetics, not structural or thermal performance.

questions.text: What is the total minimum thickness of Portland cement plaster applied over concrete hollow block (CHB) in Philippine practice under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215?

options.text: 22–27 mm (3-coat system)
15–20 mm exterior / 12–15 mm interior (2-coat system over masonry)
9–13 mm (2-coat gypsum system)
12–15 mm total (thin-coat polymer-modified plaster)

questions.rationale: CHB + cement plaster is the dominant wall system in Philippine construction. The 2-coat system over masonry is standard: base coat (leveling) + finish coat (surface). No scratch coat because the masonry surface provides mechanical bond.

questions.text: What type of plaster is appropriate for exterior applications and wet areas under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215?

options.text: Gypsum plaster — it sets quickly and provides a smooth finish suitable for exterior exposure, although it lacks water resistance.
Portland cement plaster — it cures by hydration and is water-resistant after full cure, making it suitable for exterior and wet areas
Keene's cement — its hardness and density make it the preferred exterior plaster in tropical climates, despite its limited use.
Lime plaster — its carbonation setting process makes it ideal for wet environments, although it is less durable than cement-based plasters.

questions.rationale: Material compatibility is a core principle: gypsum = interior only (water-soluble); Portland cement = exterior and wet areas. Using the wrong plaster type in the wrong environment causes premature failure.

questions.text: In which type of construction is wood lath permitted under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215, and why is it not permitted elsewhere?

options.text: Wood lath is permitted in Type I (combustible) construction only; it is classified as combustible and incompatible with fire-resistive requirements in Types II–V
Wood lath is permitted in all construction types as long as it is treated with fire-retardant coating, which is a common misconception
Wood lath is permitted in Types I and II construction; Types III–V require metal lath due to stricter fire safety standards
Wood lath is prohibited in all types of construction under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215, which is not accurate for Type I construction

questions.rationale: Wood lath is historical in Philippine practice. Its combustibility classification bars it from any construction type requiring fire-resistive ratings. Modern construction uses gypsum lath or metal lath in fire-resistive applications.

questions.text: What is the minimum thickness of gypsum board used as a base for 2-coat gypsum plaster, and what type of lath provides this substrate under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1215?

options.text: 12.7 mm gypsum board; gypsum lath, which is standard for most applications
9.5–12.7 mm gypsum lath (paper-faced gypsum board)
15.9 mm Type X gypsum board; metal lath, which is used for fire-rated assemblies
9.5 mm regular gypsum board; metal lath, typically used in non-load bearing partitions

questions.rationale: Gypsum lath is distinct from gypsum wall board (drywall). It is specifically designed as a plaster base, with paper facing engineered for plaster bond, not for direct decoration.

questions.text: A 3-coat plaster system is specified for an interior wall. What is the acceptable total thickness range under PD 1096 Sec. 1215?

options.text: 9 to 13 millimeters total thickness for a 3-coat plaster system
15 to 20 millimeters total thickness for a 3-coat plaster system
22 to 27 millimeters total thickness for a 3-coat plaster system
30 to 38 millimeters total thickness for a 3-coat plaster system

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 specifies that a 3-coat plaster system must have a total thickness between 22mm and 27mm. The 2-coat system has a different, thinner range of 9 to 13mm.
questions.explanation: The 22–27mm range for 3-coat plaster accommodates the scratch coat (approximately 9–10mm), brown coat (approximately 8–10mm), and finish coat (approximately 3–5mm). The range allows field variation while ensuring minimum total thickness for durability and fire resistance contribution. The thinner 2-coat system (9–13mm) is only appropriate where fire resistance contribution from the plaster is not required.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Sec. 1215, wood lath is restricted to use in which building construction type only?

options.text: Wood lath is permitted in Type I and Type II construction only
Wood lath is permitted in Type I construction only
Wood lath is permitted in all construction types for interior partitions
Wood lath is permitted in Type I through Type III construction

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 restricts the use of wood lath as a plaster base to Type I construction only. More fire-resistive construction types (Type II through Type V) require non-combustible lath materials such as metal lath or gypsum board.
questions.explanation: Wood lath is a combustible material. Its restriction to Type I construction (the least fire-resistive Philippine building type) is consistent with the overall code logic: combustible building components are only permitted in construction types where other combustible elements are already accepted. In Type II through Type V buildings, non-combustible lath is required to maintain fire resistance ratings.

questions.text: For which specific interior environment does PD 1096 Sec. 1215 designate Keene's cement plaster as the appropriate finish?

options.text: Keene's cement is specified for high-temperature kitchen and laundry areas
Keene's cement is specified for high-humidity interior areas such as bathrooms
Keene's cement is specified for high-traffic areas requiring abrasion-resistant finish
Keene's cement is specified for fire-rated assemblies requiring non-combustible finish

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 designates Keene's cement plaster for use in high-humidity interior areas such as bathrooms and shower rooms. Keene's cement (anhydrous calcium sulfate with alum) produces a dense, hard, moisture-resistant finish surface.
questions.explanation: Keene's cement is a specialized gypsum product that, unlike regular gypsum plaster, has been processed to resist moisture absorption. It is still an interior-only material (gypsum-based) but is appropriate for humid interior environments. Its use in bathrooms addresses the problem of regular gypsum plaster deteriorating in wet room conditions without requiring the full switch to cement plaster.

questions.text: What is the minimum weight per square meter specified in PD 1096 Sec. 1215 for metal lath used as a plaster base?

options.text: 1.6 kilograms per square meter minimum weight for metal lath
2.0 kilograms per square meter minimum weight for metal lath
2.4 kilograms per square meter minimum weight for metal lath
3.2 kilograms per square meter minimum weight for metal lath

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 specifies that metal lath used as a plaster base must have a minimum weight of 2.4 kg/m². This weight requirement ensures sufficient mechanical key depth for the scratch coat to bond adequately.
questions.explanation: The 2.4 kg/m² minimum weight for metal lath corresponds to the standard expanded metal diamond mesh lath widely available in the Philippine market. Lighter lath has shallower diamond openings, reducing the mechanical interlock surface area available for the scratch coat plaster to bond into, leading to delamination failure.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Sec. 1215, what is the total thickness range permitted for a 2-coat plaster system?

options.text: 6 to 9 millimeters total thickness for a 2-coat plaster system
9 to 13 millimeters total thickness for a 2-coat plaster system
15 to 19 millimeters total thickness for a 2-coat plaster system
20 to 25 millimeters total thickness for a 2-coat plaster system

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 specifies a total thickness range of 9 to 13mm for 2-coat plaster systems. This is substantially thinner than the 22–27mm required for 3-coat systems.
questions.explanation: A 2-coat system omits the scratch coat, reducing total thickness. The 9–13mm range covers a base coat (6–9mm) plus a finish coat (3–4mm). Two-coat plaster is appropriate over smooth concrete or masonry substrates that provide adequate mechanical bond without the scratch coat keying required over metal lath.

questions.text: What is the nominal thickness of Type X gypsum board as specified under PD 1096 Sec. 1215?

options.text: 12.7 millimeters nominal thickness for Type X gypsum board
15.9 millimeters nominal thickness for Type X gypsum board
19.0 millimeters nominal thickness for Type X gypsum board
25.4 millimeters nominal thickness for Type X gypsum board

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 specifies Type X gypsum board at a nominal thickness of 15.9mm. Type X board contains glass fibers that slow the calcination process during fire, providing enhanced fire resistance compared to standard gypsum board.
questions.explanation: The 15.9mm (approximately 5/8 inch) thickness for Type X gypsum board is the standard fire-rated thickness used in 1-hour and 2-hour fire-rated assemblies. Regular gypsum board is typically 12.7mm (1/2 inch). The additional 3.2mm thickness plus the glass fiber reinforcement of Type X board provides the extended fire resistance needed for rated assemblies.

questions.text: PD 1096 Sec. 1215 restricts the use of gypsum plaster to interior applications only. Which plaster type is required for exterior wall surfaces?

options.text: Lime putty plaster is required for all exterior surfaces
Cement plaster (stucco) is required for exterior wall applications
Gypsum plaster may be used exterior with a waterproofing admixture added
Acrylic finish plaster is the code-required exterior plaster type

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 restricts gypsum plaster to interior use only and requires cement plaster (stucco) for exterior surfaces. Gypsum is hygroscopic and deteriorates rapidly when exposed to moisture, making it unsuitable for exterior applications.
questions.explanation: Gypsum (calcium sulfate) dissolves in water over time, making it incompatible with exterior exposure in the Philippine climate, which includes heavy seasonal rainfall. Cement plaster (Portland cement, sand, water) is alkaline and weather-resistant. This exterior/interior division is absolute in Sec. 1215 — there is no provision for waterproofed gypsum as an exterior substitute.

questions.text: A contractor proposes using metal lath weighing 2.0 kg/m² for a plaster wall assembly in a Type II building. The architect accepts this substitution. Which party has violated PD 1096 Sec. 1215, and what is the nature of the violation?

options.text: Only the contractor violated the code by supplying undersized lath material, which does not meet the minimum weight requirement
Only the architect violated the code by accepting a non-compliant substitution, failing to ensure code compliance
Both parties share responsibility; the lath weight of 2.0 kg/m² is below the 2.4 kg/m² minimum
Neither party violated the code because 2.0 kg/m² is within the acceptable tolerance range, as per their interpretation

questions.rationale: Sec. 1215 specifies a minimum metal lath weight of 2.4 kg/m². A 2.0 kg/m² lath falls 16.7% below this minimum. Both the contractor (proposing non-compliant material) and the architect (approving it) share responsibility for the code violation.
questions.explanation: Professional responsibility under PD 1096 does not rest solely with the contractor. The architect of record is responsible for reviewing and approving material substitutions for code compliance. Accepting 2.0 kg/m² lath when the code requires 2.4 kg/m² minimum is a professional error. There is no tolerance provision in Sec. 1215 — 2.4 kg/m² is a hard minimum, not a target with allowable deviation.

questions.text: An architect specifies a 3-coat gypsum plaster system with a total thickness of 19mm on interior corridor walls of a Type III building. Which code violation, if any, exists in this specification?

options.text: No violation: 19mm falls within the 3-coat system range and Type III permits gypsum plaster
Thickness violation only: 19mm is below the 22mm minimum for a 3-coat system
Thickness violation only: 19mm exceeds the 13mm maximum for any gypsum plaster application
Two violations: 19mm is below the 22mm minimum for 3-coat, and the lath must be non-combustible for Type III

questions.rationale: The specification has one violation: 19mm is below the 22mm minimum required for a 3-coat plaster system under Sec. 1215. Gypsum plaster is permitted on interior walls of any construction type, and 19mm is not outside any absolute limit — it simply falls short of the 3-coat minimum of 22mm.
questions.explanation: The 19mm thickness is between the 2-coat maximum (13mm) and the 3-coat minimum (22mm) — it satisfies neither system's requirements. If the designer intends a 2-coat system, maximum thickness is 13mm; if a 3-coat system, minimum is 22mm. The gypsum material is acceptable for Type III interior use; the violation is solely the incorrect thickness for the specified number of coats.

questions.text: A hospital bathroom is being finished with 3-coat plaster. The specification calls for gypsum scratch and brown coats (total 20mm) with a Keene's cement finish coat (4mm), totaling 24mm. Evaluate this specification against PD 1096 Sec. 1215.

options.text: Fully compliant: total 24mm is within the 3-coat range, Keene's cement is appropriate for bathrooms
Non-compliant: Keene's cement cannot be used with gypsum base coats in a 3-coat system
Non-compliant: total 24mm exceeds the 22mm maximum for 3-coat systems in institutional buildings
Non-compliant: hospital bathrooms require cement plaster throughout, not gypsum base coats

questions.rationale: This specification fully complies with Sec. 1215: the total thickness of 24mm falls within the 22–27mm range for 3-coat systems, and Keene's cement is the code-designated finish for high-humidity interior areas such as hospital bathrooms. Keene's cement is compatible with gypsum base coats as a system.
questions.explanation: This question tests simultaneous application of three Sec. 1215 provisions: (1) total thickness for 3-coat systems (22–27mm — satisfied at 24mm), (2) Keene's cement for humid interiors (satisfied for hospital bathrooms), and (3) gypsum plaster restriction to interior use (satisfied — this is an interior bathroom). The use of gypsum base coats with a Keene's cement finish coat is a standard and code-compliant approach. Cement plaster throughout would also be compliant but is not required.
